Prof teaching is good, explained clearly with steps.
=================================================
No lecture video is provided for this semester (prof said it is classroom issue???) make it hard to do revison if you don't go class.

No assignment solution will be provided and you can only know your overall score so you will not know which question you did wrong in assignment and will make the same mistake in midterm !!!!

The only support you can have is the Q&A Tutorial that hold only once !! where you can ask question about your hw.

Email reply from TA:

Thank you for your email.
Please note that the assignment solutions will not be released. To support students in preparing for the final exam and clarifying assignment-related questions, we previously held a discussion/review section on 12/5 where students were encouraged to ask questions about the assignments and their solutions.

If you have any specific questions about the topics, you are also welcome to send them to us, and we will do our best to help.

==========================================
Overall, Teaching is good but lack of supporting.

sections.content:
MANY topics
U can refer to other reviews as I dont think Prof. Albert removed/added much.

Plus Professor teaches each quite long (often overrun), so some of the last topics might be rushed/skipped.

My learning is that many methods are iterative. So sometimes professor will explain about computationally expensive/cheap or time complexity , since he taught algorithm before. However, since I didn't take 3711, I am confused for those parts.

Some topics are related to other ML topics like PCA/CNN , so if u have taken courses like Prof DY's comp4211 it would be beneficial, but not a must.

Also, Professor said many of those methods/papers were state of the art/golden standard for many years, but replaced by deep learning recently. So this course introduces some more "Classical" methods , still useable but maybe not the most up to date. For those, i think 4471 / elec4240 covers more on deep learning.

Don’t expect 4421 be very AI as in neural network stuff, but u will be working with many matrices (raw) instead
sections.teaching:
Professor Albert Chung is very knoweldgeable with yrs of experience in this field, research + worked with industry. And in class, he is nice to answer students who raise questions in class/after class. His teaching style is decent , where he draws many diagrams on the board and some jokes here and there. Or I should say, if you dont attend lecture and just read notes, u might not understand some parts, since he leaves some pages blank intentionally.

However he is very busy. So, the Helpful TAs are all very nice.
If you have questions, reach out to them in person/email and they will reply in detail. I recommend you to ask the TAs first before asking Professor.

sections.content:
A standard introduction to image processing techniques.

Frankly speaking, the course is like an overview on the techniques related to image processing. So, it is easier than a typical level 4 elective. That is also why it has an extremely high mean/median score.

However, if we are to consider the number of chapters in the course and the semester duration, I would say that the content is rather appropriate.

Chapters include the following:

Introduction
Image Fundamentals
Image Transformations
Image Filtering
Image Restoration
Image Compression
Morphological Image Processing
Image Segmentation
Image Registration
Feature Extraction
Image Recognition and Deep Learning
Advanced Topics in Medical Image Processing
sections.teaching:
Professor Chen speaks rather fast, so it is a bit hard to follow when in the lecture room, since notes are released just a day early.
But luckily, lectures videos are present in canvas. Once you read  the notes and watch the videos, it is easy to understand.
sections.grading:
The mean/median of this course is high, like really high for assignments and midterms. So you need to be careful about your answers.

This is especially true for assignments where some questions are kinda out of lecture scope. To be fair, they do provide hints for questions like that.

Finals, on the other hand, provide more flexibility since mean/median is more "typical".

To break it down:
Assignment 1 (10%): Median 94, High 100
Assignment 2 (10%): Median 100, High 100
Assignment 3 (10%): Median 100, High 100
Midterm (30%): Median 82, High 100
Final Exam (40%): Median 75, High 97

My weighted overall is around 95, which translates to an A+.

Some questions in exam relate to details mentioned in small font/images (like the phase angle) and are easy to be missed. So, do remember to clearly look at the images and their labels because they may be asked in exam.
sections.workload:
The only workload comes from the assignment, which should take about two hours or three if you are unfamiliar with the lecture notes and less if you are familiar.
Given that each assignment has just 4-5 questions, I would say the workload is appropriate.

That said, you will likely need to study the lecture notes in depth.

sections.content:
Basic introduction image processing, including spatial domain, frequency domain, image restoration and filtering, morphological image processing, image segmentation, image registration, image compression,  face recognition, etc.

All very practical and is generally interesting.
sections.teaching:
Decent.

Heavy accent however he is very enthusiastic about the lecture contents, so therefore the lectures were not too bad, however he still repeats off the powerpoint quite a lot, and since attendance is not counted a lot of people ended up skipping.

Tutorials go over using MATLAB for image processing, however the homework and exams do not cover the contents this semester, so only attend if you are interested.
sections.grading:
Acceptable for COMP standards.

30% Midterm: Questions that are basically the same as ones seen in assignments, however it is easy to make careless mistakes, so be careful! Averages are very high (79/100)

40% Final: Exactly the same as the midterm, all based on assignments and therefore averages are again very high (73.5/100)

30% Assignments: 3 assignments, each worth 10%, most questions can be answered by looking into the lecture notes, and for those that cannot, answers can be found on the internet, averages are almost full mark on all 3.

The complex math shown in the lectures ended up being very basic and easy calculations, so this course is more about being careful and studying the assignments.

0.5% less than mean overall, B-, as expected.
sections.workload:
Quite low for a 4000 level course.

Assignments are very easy and takes less than a day to complete, and for the exams since none of the tutorial content is covered and all questions are based on assignments and lecture notes, studying for the exam is also not too difficult.

sections.content:
The content is interesting. It taught some basic techniques in  image processing. The final project was either a survey project or a research project, which I chose to evaluate existing methods or to propose new methods on a problem in the research one.

Introduction to image processing. Topics include image processing and analysis in spatial and frequency domains, image restoration and compression, image segmentation and registration, morphological image processing, representation and description, object recognition, related application areas and some other closely related topics. Some sophisticated image processing and analysis tools and state-of-the-art methods may also be introduced subject to the availability of time.
sections.teaching: It was the first time the professor taught this course. The professor was passionate in delivering the course. He tried to encourage interaction in class. Also, he is a kind person and considerate to the students; at one time, he postponed the deadline the final project to provide the students more breathing time. However, he does not speak good English, which may affect how the students understand the materials.
sections.grading: The assignments and exams were a bit too easy and could not differentiate the students' grades too much. The grading of the project might have a greater impact. I did not do pretty well in the group project, even I have good scores in the exams, I received B range at the end.
sections.workload: There were a total of three assignments. The questions were straightforward, and the length is acceptable, each just took me as much as a day to finish. The mid-term and final were super EAZY. Some of the questions are just variants of the ones in the assignments. However, the group project needed some considerable amount of effort and time.

sections.content: This course covers some basic and interesting topic on image processing, including spatial domain, frequency domain, image restoration and filtering, morphological image processing, image segmentation, image registration, image compression,  face recognition, etc.
sections.teaching: Prof. Chung is an expert in this area. He can explain the concepts clearly at good pace. He is also nice and chats with students after the course. TAs are also very helpful and respond quickly to my questions on assignment, even I asked during weekend.
sections.grading: I got an excellent grading from this course I have pretty good result in the final exam but I can't finish the second assignment. So this course does not require students to be perfect.
sections.workload: There are 3 assignments and final exam. The first 2 assignments consist of many questions and some high level programming to test your concepts of image processing. The difficulty of the last assignment is tuned to be much easier as many students could barely finish the second one. I appreciate that the difficulty of assignment is adjusted according to the ability and tight of schedule.
